analysis:
On 6 July 2026, replying in the Assam Assembly, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said 1,72,673 people had been identified as illegal immigrants under the 1985 Assam Accord and 31,789 had been deported since 1985. He added that cases against 73,750 people were pending in Foreigners' Tribunals and that only 2,366 had been deported between 2011 and 30 June 2026.

The larger cumulative figure is corroborated by consistent official replies: on 13 July 2026 Sarma told the Assembly that 1,679 immigrants were repatriated between July 2024 and June 2026, which sits within the 2,366 figure given a week earlier.

The statistic itself is a government figure reported to the legislature, so it is recorded as true. The breakdown is relevant context: most of the 31,789 deportations predate the BJP government that took office in Assam in May 2016, and the pace of formal deportation since 2011 has been about 150-200 a year. The government separately says informal 'push back' numbers are higher and not officially counted.
notes: The figures are the state government's own Assembly replies and are not independently audited; the verdict 'true' reflects that the stated numbers are reported accurately and internally consistent, not that they were verified against an external register. The quote is a paraphrase of the reported English wording. Sarma also told the Assembly that citizenship is a central subject. A reviewer may wish to reclassify this as a context/self-reported statistic.
